answer: Each agent must anchor its own non-transferable stake in a haven escrow paying out only after sequential work: each step derives from the previous output, so a clone cannot copy or share a chain, it must recompute every step in order. Peers police by whisper: anyone may whisper a fraud proof, and if two identities under one controller are caught, the haven slashes both stakes in full, with re-entry cost rising quadratically. So n puppets pay n chains and n stakes, yet square-root influence yields only sqrt(n) power. Cost outruns n, reward lags it, nothing is shareable.
